CANDIDATES.DUPLICATE_RISK: MEDIUM: dynamic reload/reconciliation is an established production pattern, but generation fencing + atomic publication + state migration + drain/recovery + bounded telemetry form a distinct coupled work package.
EDGE_FAILURE_SURFACE: invalid update mixed with valid membership change
backend disappearance during an active request
stale affinity to an ineligible backend
CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Implement generation-safe dynamic route and upstream reconciliation so configuration and backend-membership changes apply atomically under concurrent traffic, rolling backend turnover, invalid updates, and process restart.
CANDIDATES.INHERITED_SYSTEM_STATE: A solver-visible Go edge-routing runtime with public HTTP entrypoints, dynamic configuration, multiple upstream pools, regional discovery/configuration, persistent checkpoint state, and operational documentation; no private topology or verifier behavior is assumed.
CANDIDATES.INSTRUCTION_FIT: The material end state fits naturally within roughly 10–12 concise responsibility-level bullets; architecture/protocol details can remain in normal solver-visible documentation.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Rebuilding all selection and sticky state on every reload makes reload correctness operationally unstable.
Publishing routes before referenced pools creates mixed-generation serving.
Syntax validation without generation fencing permits stale updates to win races.
Immediate backend removal can strand in-flight traffic.
Checkpointing metadata before the full runtime generation is durable can recover a state that was never safely published.
Retired endpoint metrics or transports can leak indefinitely.
CANDIDATES.PERSONA: Edge platform engineer or SRE responsible for a public-facing Go HTTP edge-routing runtime.
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: In-flight and long-lived requests remain valid across unrelated updates.
Unchanged route semantics remain stable across generations.
Healthy unchanged endpoints preserve meaningful runtime state.
Rejected updates cannot damage the serving generation.
Readers never observe partially applied configuration.
Runtime and observability state remain bounded after repeated updates.
REFERENCES: Caddy reverse_proxy documentation: dynamic upstreams, load balancing, active/passive health checks, streaming and transports
Traefik HTTP load-balancing/service documentation: dynamic routing configuration, health checks and sticky sessions
Current Caddy reverse-proxy issue inventory demonstrates continuing production coupling among upstream identity, health state, transport and request semantics
REQUIRED_END_STATE: Validate and compile candidate configuration into immutable runtime snapshots before publication.
Fence accepted generations so stale or out-of-order updates cannot overwrite newer state.
Publish route and upstream state atomically, preserving a last-known-good generation on invalid updates.
Reconcile endpoint additions, removals, and unchanged endpoints by stable runtime identity.
Preserve reusable load-balancing, affinity, health, and lifecycle state for unchanged endpoints.
Drain removed endpoints before retirement while excluding them from new routing and retries.
Checkpoint and recover the latest complete accepted generation without mixed or partially restored state.
Retire unreachable runtime objects, transports, affinity entries, and telemetry without unbounded growth.
REQUIREMENT_FAMILIES: observability lifecycle and metric garbage collection

SCALE_FIT.P2P_SURFACE: Strong preservation surface for last-known-good serving, unchanged routes/endpoints, in-flight traffic, and bounded state.
SCALE_FIT.SUBSTANTIVE_RUNTIME_LOC: Naturally supports well above the 3,000 substantive reachable LOC floor across differentiated runtime modules.

Apply deterministic health transitions with decay/recovery rules.

outputs.DUPLICATE_RISK_NOTES: Current public reverse-proxy documentation and issue patterns confirm dynamic-upstream, health, transport and state-lifecycle concerns are real production work. The recommended package does not copy public prose or reduce to a generic reload bug; its distinctive scope is the atomic generation/state-migration/drain/recovery lifecycle. No large primary-record dataset is required because the runtime is configuration/state backed rather than a data-backed business-record workload.
outputs.WHY_THIS_ONE: This candidate has the strongest strict-profile fit without padding. Every requirement participates in one versioned runtime-state transition: validate/compile -> fence generation -> reconcile/migrate state -> atomically publish -> serve -> drain/retire -> checkpoint/recover. That coupling naturally yields differentiated runtime responsibilities, 20–30 interrelated manifestations, 25–30 distinct F2P scenarios plus preservation coverage, and credible concurrency/restart/failure surfaces while keeping the material work request concise.
